header: L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: Close: all 7 Status A or M findings of round 9 read as resolved at d458f83; the delta adds one omission (B6 outside the plan's required results) and one probe predicate that cannot go red, plus two advisories.

findings.defect: The round-9 write pass added probe B6 and says each of B1 to B6 is a block B result, but the plan's O6 row and the T092 acceptance still require-pass B1 to B5 plus C2 to C6, and 11 11.2 still sizes the sitting as 'B1 to B5'.
findings.scenario: The release candidate's block B sitting skips B6 or records it as fail; `tools/ci probes --require-pass B1,B2,B3,B4,B5,C2,...` exits 0, the acceptance PR merges, and the replay that guards the fake sbx against a drifted candidate sbx never gated anything.
findings.change: Add B6 to every require-pass list and 'B1 to B5' phrase of plan.md O6 and T092 (and the O7 rows if B6 is meant to be rerun), and to the time estimate of 11 11.2; or say why B6 is outside the required set.

findings.defect: B2 now includes 'a commit made with the key added by ssh-add -c asks for confirmation through the installed askpass and is signed', but B2 is kind: check with a machine predicate, and a prompt shown to a human is not an observation the harness can make; 05 5.4 says macOS ships no askpass, so the clause cannot say where the askpass runs.
findings.scenario: On a Mac with no askpass the commit is signed or refused for a reason the probe does not read; the harness records pass on 'is signed' alone, 05 5.4 stops saying confirm-on-use is unproven, and the property (a confirmation was asked) was never observed.
findings.change: State the observation: either the harness reads the askpass program's invocation (a marker its askpass wrapper writes) as the evidence that a confirmation was asked, or mark that half **[review]** with the maintainer's reading under the result; and say on which host the askpass sits.

findings.defect: The refusal now requires the latest scheduled fuzz.yml run's head commit to be an ancestor of the release commit with no tagged-guard file changed since, but the spec states no cadence for the schedule and no way to produce a qualifying run (a workflow_dispatch run is not scheduled).
findings.scenario: A guard moves on main the day before the rc tag; release.yml refuses until the next scheduled run, whose date no page states, so the maintainer cannot tell a wait from a failure and may be tempted to edit the check.
findings.change: Name the schedule in 10 10.1 (the fuzz row) and say a manual run of fuzz.yml counts or does not, in one sentence next to step 1.

findings.section: 10 10.2 (pr job row; The pr step paragraph); plan.md T005
findings.defect: The pr job runs only on GitHub under pull_request_target and fetches the head by head.sha without credentials; the grammar fixtures cover the workflow shape, but nothing says how the first real run, or a pull request from a fork whose sha may not be fetchable that way, is observed.
findings.scenario: The pr task lands green on unit tests, the job fails at its fetch on the first fork PR or reads an empty range and passes every PR, and the required check is a job that proves nothing.
findings.change: Add to T005 an acceptance line that its pull request's Evidence holds the job's log for a same-repo PR and one with the head unreachable (refusal), and say the pr step fails when the walk finds zero commits.
